en: Udāna 4.2 Uddhatasutta Thus have I heard:
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Kusinārā in the Upavattana, the sal-tree grove of the Mallas. Now at that time,
a number of bhikkhus were dwelling not far from the Blessed One in a forest hut—
restless, arrogant, fickle, talkative, with scattered speech, muddled mindfulness, lacking clear comprehension, unconcentrated, with wandering minds, and with unrestrained faculties.

The Blessed One saw those many bhikkhus dwelling not far from the forest hut—arrogant, conceited, fickle, talkative, loose in speech, muddled in mindfulness, lacking clear comprehension, unconcentrated, with wandering minds, and with unrestrained senses.
Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired exclamation (udāna):
And by one struck down by wrong view,
one falls under the power of Māra.
Therefore, for one whose mind is guarded,
Having understood arising and passing away,
the bhikkhu who has overcome sloth and torpor abandons all states of woe.
